extracted.intended_audience: bioinformatics researchers and genomics investigators seeking databases and tools for gene-list functional analysis
extracted.subtask_description: Evaluating or selecting a biological database/catalog entry (here: DAVID) based on metadata, coverage, tools, programmatic access, provenance, and usability for gene-list functional analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accessibility
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicates whether the database is reachable and usable (openly accessible vs. restricted). The page explicitly marks DAVID as 'Accessible' and provides the live URL for direct access.

rubrics_metrics.name: Currency and versioning
rubrics_metrics.description: Year founded: 2003; Last update: 2022-2-19; Version: version6.8
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recency of updates and explicit version identifiers are used to assess maintenance and currency. The entry lists founding year, last update date, and version string (version6.8).

rubrics_metrics.name: Data type and data objects covered
rubrics_metrics.description: Data type: DNA; Data object: Animal, Archaea, Bacteria, Fungi, Plant
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scope of the underlying data (type and biological object classes) is a key quality dimension — here DAVID covers DNA-level annotations across multiple kingdoms (animals, microbes, plants, fungi).

rubrics_metrics.name: Database category / functional scope
rubrics_metrics.description: Database category: Pathway; Standard ontology and nomenclature
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Categorization (e.g., pathway database, ontology/nomenclature resource) helps determine fit for a research task. DAVID is categorized as both a pathway resource and a standard-ontology/nomenclature resource.

rubrics_metrics.name: Species and taxonomy coverage
rubrics_metrics.description: Major species: Homo sapiens; Mus musculus. The DAVID Gene system increased taxonomy coverage from 17,399 to 55,464.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Breadth of organism coverage — number of species/taxonomic entries supported — affects applicability. The entry and paper abstracts emphasize a large increase in taxonomy coverage and list key model species.

rubrics_metrics.name: Functional annotation tools and analysis features
rubrics_metrics.description: Provides 'a comprehensive set of functional annotation tools for investigators to understand biological meaning behind large list of genes.' Tools include gene functional classification, functional annotation chart or clustering, functional_annotation_table, GO/KEGG/Domain charts, visualization, clustering into biological modules, pathway viewing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluates the analytic functionality offered: enrichment analysis, classification, clustering, visualization, pathway mapping, dynamic linking to external repositories. The page lists multiple specific tool suites (Annotation Tool, GoCharts, KeggCharts, DomainCharts, Gene Functional Classification Tool).

rubrics_metrics.name: Integration of external annotation sources
rubrics_metrics.description: Incorporated annotations include small molecule-gene interactions from PubChem, drug-gene interactions from DrugBank, tissue expression from Human Protein Atlas, disease information from DisGeNET, pathways from WikiPathways and PathBank. 'more than 40 publicly available functional annotation sources' are integrated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Breadth and diversity of integrated external resources (databases and annotation types) is a metric of coverage and richness. The entry names numerous integrated sources and states the Knowledgebase centralizes many public resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Programmatic access / web services
rubrics_metrics.description: DAVID-WS: a stateful web service to facilitate gene/protein list analysis. Sample clients provided in Java, Perl, Python and Matlab. Web service and sample clients are freely available under the DAVID License.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Availability and quality of APIs/web services (stateful vs stateless, client libraries, URL limits) determine automation capability. The DAVID-WS description explains purpose, stateful behavior, and example clients.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identifier conversion / ID mapping capability
rubrics_metrics.description: DAVID gene ID conversion tool (DICT) converts user's input gene or gene product identifiers from one type to another using an enhanced ID-ID mapping database.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Support for high-throughput identifier conversion and robust ID mapping is crucial for practical usage of heterogeneous gene lists. The page highlights the DICT as a dedicated tool addressing this bottleneck.

rubrics_metrics.name: Knowledgebase downloadability and data accessibility
rubrics_metrics.description: The entire DAVID Knowledgebase is freely downloadable or searchable at the DAVID site.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Whether the underlying data/knowledgebase can be downloaded for offline or bulk analysis is a key reproducibility and reusability criterion. The entry explicitly states the knowledgebase is downloadable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication record and provenance
rubrics_metrics.description: Multiple citable publications are listed (e.g., 'DAVID: a web server for functional enrichment analysis…' PMID: 35325185 and earlier core papers), with abstracts describing updates and methods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scholarly publications describing the resource provide provenance, methods, and credibility. The page lists many PMIDs and abstracts summarizing the resource's development and methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bibliometrics and citation impact
rubrics_metrics.description: Ranking metrics shown: 'All databases: 1/6932 (100%)', 'Pathway: 1/455 (100%)', 'Standard ontology and nomenclature: 1/239 (100%)'; '54,950 Citations', '2,389.13 z-index'. Individual paper citation counts are shown alongside PMIDs (e.g., 4309 Citations for the 2022 Nucleic Acids Res. paper).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aggregate citation numbers, z-index, and category rankings are used as proxies of community impact and adoption. The entry provides both per-publication citation counts and aggregate ranking metrics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Community reviews and rating
rubrics_metrics.description: Community reviews: 2.9 Stars (5). Review facets listed: Data quality & quantity; Content organization & presentation; System accessibility & reliability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: User/community ratings and reviews provide qualitative feedback on usability, reliability, and data quality. The page shows an overall star rating and named review facets (though detailed numeric facet scores are not shown).

rubrics_metrics.name: Content organization and presentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Listed as a review/evaluation facet: 'Content organization & presentation'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: How well content is organized, labeled, and presented affects discoverability and user experience. This facet is explicitly listed among community review categories for the database.

rubrics_metrics.name: System accessibility and reliability
rubrics_metrics.description: Listed as a review/evaluation facet: 'System accessibility & reliability'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operational reliability, uptime, and responsive interfaces/API behavior are important for production use. This is one of the named community review facets on the entry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data quality and quantity
rubrics_metrics.description: Listed as a review/evaluation facet: 'Data quality & quantity'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measures of annotation completeness, accuracy, and the volume of records (gene-term records, coverage across annotation types) are key. The page highlights that the number of gene-term records for most annotation types 'have significantly increased' following updates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institutional ownership and contact/maintenance
rubrics_metrics.description: University/Institution: National Cancer Institute. Address: Laboratory of Immunopathogenesis and Bioinformatics, National Cancer Institute, Frederick, MD. Contact name: DAVID Bioinformatic Team. Contact email: weizhong.chang@nih.gov
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Information about the hosting institution, PI/team, and contact details indicates stewardship, support channels, and accountability for maintenance and updates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Licensing and terms of availability
rubrics_metrics.description: The web service and sample clients are 'made freely available under the DAVID License.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Licensing terms (free availability, license type/restrictions) affect reuse, redistribution, and integration into pipelines. The entry notes explicit DAVID licensing for the web service and clients.

rubrics_metrics.name: Algorithms and methodological features
rubrics_metrics.description: The DAVID Gene Functional Classification Tool 'uses a novel agglomeration algorithm to condense a list of genes or associated biological terms into organized classes of related genes or biology, called biological modules.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The presence and description of underlying algorithms (e.g., agglomeration/module-centric clustering) inform users about methodological strengths, assumptions, and how results are produced and should be interpreted.
